purpose: Alendronate is used to treat and prevent osteoporosis, which is a condition where your bones become weak and brittle. It is also used to treat bone loss caused by steroids and a condition called Paget's disease of the bone. It helps lower your risk of breaking a bone, especially in your hip or spine.
how_it_works: Your body is constantly breaking down old bone and building new bone. In osteoporosis, your body breaks down bone faster than it can rebuild it, making your bones weaker. Alendronate works by slowing down the cells that break bone apart, which helps your bones stay stronger and denser over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and irritation or pain in your esophagus (the tube connecting your throat to your stomach). You may also experience muscle, joint, or bone pain. Some people get headaches or mild stomach upset.
warnings: You must take this medication first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of plain water — not coffee, juice, or mineral water. Stay sitting upright or standing for at least 30 minutes after taking it and do not eat or drink anything else during that time. This helps prevent serious irritation or ulcers in your esophagus. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, low calcium levels, or trouble swallowing. Rarely, it can cause jaw bone problems or unusual thigh bone fractures with long-term use.
typical_dosing: The most common dose for osteoporosis is 70 mg taken once a week, or 10 mg taken once daily. It must always be taken first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full 8-ounce glass of plain water. Do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking it and wait at least 30 minutes before eating or drinking anything else.
